rv.q: Director/Choreographer Brenda Didier has given the music of Jimmy Buffett an energetic and colorful telling.
This show will take you far from your concerns and drop you back in Skokie heading to the parking garage with a giant smile on your face.
The Buffett musical is a light, good-natured escape that provides an unruffled evening - an inviting couple of hours of coastal fun.
It’s pure escapist entertainment and nothing more.
The show is like an adult recess from life’s pressures.
Didier knows how to turn material that relies on easy tropes into engaging and solid entertainment.
Despite some great singing voices and the warm atmosphere, some viewers may find issues with the musical’s cringy humor and underdeveloped writing.
Playful and fun, “Escape to Margaritaville” is a jukebox musical which brings together Jimmy Buffett’s songs in a lighthearted story about budding romances.
The jokes are rolling in from lost pop tops, to innuendos, to puns that the cast delivers in this light-hearted musical.

cn.t: Critics find this lighthearted jukebox musical a pleasant, beach-themed escape with strong vocals and energetic choreography, though the thin plot and humor work best for devoted Parrotheads rather than general audiences.
